\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize Outcome: overall liberalism, mean over the three LLMs (as in Tables 4--8). OLS: the outcome on the populism score of model $x$ alone; IV: the same regression with the populism score of model $x$ instrumented by that of model $z$ (two-stage least squares). Both on the manifestos with all three variables (N between 2,575 and 2,817 with country and year FE, between 2,115 and 2,363 with party FE). F: first-stage Wald F statistic. $\hat\lambda$ = OLS / IV, the implied reliability of model $x$'s populism score given the fixed effects, valid if the measurement errors of the two models are independent of each other and of the outcome. Because the outcome contains model $z$'s liberalism score, scored in the same call as its populism score, a halo between the two would move the IV estimate away from zero. Last row: the populism coefficient of column (1) of Table 4 and its party-FE version, regressor = mean over the three LLMs. Standard errors clustered by party (CMP party code) in parentheses. *** p$<$0.01, ** p$<$0.05, * p$<$0.1 (IV).\end{minipage}
